name: Dengue
source: WHO WPRO dengue: "high fever ... with two of: headache, pain behind the eyes, ... muscle or joint pains, rash"

name: Malaria, early symptoms
source: WHO malaria fact sheet (Dec 2025): "The most common early symptoms of malaria are fever, headache and chills."

name: Typhoid
source: WHO typhoid fact sheet: "prolonged high fever, fatigue, headache, nausea, abdominal pain, and constipation or diarrhoea"

name: Influenza
source: WHO influenza fact sheet: "sudden onset of fever, cough (usually dry), headache, muscle and joint pain, severe malaise, sore throat and a runny nose"

name: Pneumonia
source: WHO pneumonia: "cough, shortness of breath, fever, sweating and shaking chills, fatigue, chest pain"

name: Common cold
source: CDC common cold: "sneezing, congestion, sore throat, cough ... most people with colds do not have a fever"

name: Mixed severe + mild (severe ranked first)
source: CCP requirement: prioritize severe diseases over mild ones

name: Edge: fever only
source: Edge case: a single non-specific symptom must not give a diagnosis

name: Edge: unknown symptom
source: Edge case: symptom not in the knowledge base is reported, not used

name: Dengue warning sign
source: CDC dengue: warning signs include "bleeding from the nose or gums"

name: Severe malaria
source: WHO malaria: severe symptoms include "impaired consciousness"

name: Edge: weak evidence near the threshold
source: Edge case: evidence just below the display threshold is reported as such

name: Edge: many severe symptoms but no fever
source: Edge case: in this KB fever is a required condition for every febrile disease, so no diagnosis, but red flags still fire and the missing fever is reported
